name: breeze-overlay
description: Self-hosted broadcast overlay/graphics builder — HTML5 + GSAP, serving live graphics to vMix / OBS.

scripts.//test:e2e: The config lives in tests/, so -c is required: Playwright only auto-discovers a config at the cwd root. Ad-hoc single-spec runs need it too — `pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/playwright.config.ts diagnostics` — or use test:e2e:only, which wraps it.
scripts.//lockfile: Answers the question `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` asks, without a network round trip or an install — so it can run before install in CI and fail with the package name rather than after it. Lockfile drift has broken CI twice; a developer's ordinary `pnpm install` repairs the lockfile silently, so whoever adds a dependency is the one person who never sees the problem.
scripts.//installed: The sibling question to lockfile:check, and a different one: that answers 'did someone edit a manifest without installing', this answers 'did the install happen in *this* tree'. Both fail as a bundler resolution error four gates later if unasked — and vite's suggested fix for it, externalising the module, ships an editor that throws at runtime.
scripts.//notices: Attribution for what a user actually receives, generated from the installed production tree. `notices:check` belongs in CI next to license:check: the two answer different questions — one that every source file carries its MPL notice, the other that the third-party list matches the dependencies that shipped.
scripts.//vendor: Stages GSAP into apps/server/public/vendor/. Normally run by @breeze/server's build; exposed here so it can be run on its own after changing the pin.
scripts.//release: `release:check` is CI's gate list in CI's order, run before the snapshot rather than after the push — a snapshot is the one artifact nobody re-reads before shipping. `release:copy` runs it and refuses to copy a tree that fails. Flags: --quick runs only the instant gates (nothing built, nothing written); --skip-checks skips them entirely, for re-copying a tree you just verified. The build gate is a check, not a release step — dist/ and apps/server/public are excluded from both copies — but it is load-bearing anyway, because @breeze/schema resolves to dist/ and an unbuilt tree makes the unit-test gate a test of the previous build. E2E is excluded on purpose: it needs browsers and a free port, and a gate that fails for environmental reasons is one people learn to skip.

pnpm.//: pnpm 10 blocks dependency install scripts by default — a sensible supply-chain default we keep rather than override. This list is the one pnpm honours: when the same key exists here and in pnpm-workspace.yaml, package.json wins and the workspace file's list is discarded entirely. Keep the two in sync, or entries only declared over there will keep prompting.
